entries.definition: A friendly understanding between people that makes talk feel easy.
entries.example: The volunteer built rapport with new members in minutes.

entries.definition: The set of polite rules for behavior in a social or professional setting.
entries.example: Business etiquette here includes a short handshake.

entries.definition: The official rules for how to greet or treat people in a formal setting.
entries.example: Royal protocol says who speaks first.

entries.definition: The word or phrase you use to open a conversation or a letter.
entries.example: Dear colleagues is a safe salutation in a work email.

entries.definition: Slow to show feelings or start a conversation with new people.
entries.example: He is reserved with strangers but warm with friends.

entries.definition: Enjoying meeting people and starting conversations.
entries.example: Outgoing hosts make a new club feel friendly.

entries.definition: A remark that praises someone's appearance, work, or character.
entries.example: She opened with a sincere compliment about his talk.

entries.definition: Making you feel uncomfortable or unsure what to say.
entries.example: There was an awkward silence after the wrong name.

entries.definition: To present someone again, or to present yourself after a long gap.
entries.example: Let me reintroduce the speaker before questions.

entries.definition: To fail to notice someone or something, often by accident.
entries.example: Sorry I did not wave. I did not mean to overlook you.

entries.definition: Knowing someone, but usually not very well yet.
entries.example: I am acquainted with her through the book club.

entries.definition: Warm and friendly in a polite, slightly formal way.
entries.example: Their cordial greeting put the visitors at ease.

entries.headword: I do not think we have met
entries.definition: A polite line you use when you are not sure you know someone.
entries.example: I do not think we have met. I am Hannah.

entries.definition: A formal way to present one person to another.
entries.example: Allow me to introduce our guest speaker, Professor Adeyemi.

entries.definition: An informal way to say you have not seen someone for a very long time.
entries.example: It has been ages. What have you been doing?

entries.headword: we got off on the wrong foot
entries.definition: We started a relationship badly and felt uncomfortable.
entries.example: Sorry about yesterday. I think we got off on the wrong foot.

entries.definition: To start talking with someone you have just met.
entries.example: He can strike up a conversation with almost anyone.

entries.definition: To say polite, light things like hello and how are you.
entries.example: Colleagues exchange pleasantries before the meeting starts.

entries.definition: The polite rules people follow when they meet and talk.
entries.example: Removing your shoes indoors is part of social etiquette here.

entries.definition: A small movement of the head that shows you know someone.
entries.example: She gave me a nod of recognition across the room.

entries.definition: Said when you are surprised and pleased to meet someone in an unexpected place.
entries.example: Fancy seeing you here. I thought you were still abroad.

entries.definition: Someone you recognize, which can make a new place feel safer.
entries.example: It was good to see a familiar face at the conference.

entries.definition: To feel that you do not belong in a group or situation.
entries.example: I feel out of place until someone comes over and says hello.
